transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Mina (Redwood SE), Sanjay (BrightLoop CTO), Leah (BrightLoop Lead Eng), Marco (BrightLoop PM)

Summary: Quick review of last week's sandbox run, discussed telemetry differences vs expected, looked at two failure modes (serialization and KV cache misses), proposed fallback policy (small-model + dedicated burst) and next steps for a 24h stability run. Agreed to share traces and runbook.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we got about 40 minutes, we'll do a quick run through the results you sent, then Mina will walk through a couple tuning notes and then we can align on next steps, sound good?
[00:12] Sanjay: yep that's great, thanks. quick note — we had a couple of spikes last night so I'm curious what you see on the token side versus our in-app metrics.
[00:20] Mina: super, I'll start with a short recap. from the sandbox run we saw median latency at 380ms for the 512-token typical prompt, 95th at about 1.1s. cost per 1k tokens looked roughly in the ballpark of the initial estimate, except we had higher small-request overhead due to many short-lived connections.
[00:37] Leah: yeah that matches what we saw, a lot of small requests from the mobile client, and an extra 20% at p95 where the app retried on timeouts, so multiplier effect.
[00:48] Jordan: right, retries are killing the math. two high level levers — batching and prefix/KV caching — can mitigate that, but batching only helps if you can accept a small added latency window. Mina, show the tuning notes.
[01:00] Mina: sure. first, enable continuous batching in the SDK — we have a flag in the node SDK setBatchWindowMs — even 15-20ms gives meaningful throughput gains. second, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, but note the current SDK uses 'KV cache' terminology but the telemetry sometimes prints it as 'K V cash' in the logs, so don't panic — it's the same cache. third, for short interactive flows, use streaming + chunk hooks to reduce client perceived latency.
[01:25] Marco: when you say streaming, do we need to change our proto or is it handled by the SDK by default?
[01:30] Mina: handled by SDK — you opt into streaming and register a chunk handler. small code snippet we shared in the integration guide; I'll paste again. it does require you to handle partial JSON when using structured output though.
[01:44] Leah: ah yes structured output is a pain — we hit a failure where function-calling produced truncated JSON and our parser raised and retried which made things worse.
[01:52] Sanjay: can you repeat that, truncated JSON? was that an SDK bug or a model-side issue?
[01:58] Mina: a combination. the model returned partial function call payload during a connection hiccup, the SDK will surface the chunk but we didn't have an automatic reassembly + checksum in your parser, so the app retried. easiest short-term fix: buffer chunks until you get the closing token or a checksum header we add in telemetry. long-term: we recommend using the structured-output helper in our SDK which validates JSON schema on the fly.
[02:24] Speaker 1: (mumble) yeah uh we saw that in logs too, sometimes the function name got lowercased in the transcript and mapping failed.
[02:31] Marco: that's scary — so casing issues? is that from model variation?
[02:35] Mina: yes, occasionally the model surface text casing differences, so when you map to tool hooks do case-insensitive match. we should probably add a normalization step in your parsing layer.
[02:44] Jordan: ok on durability / data controls — Sanjay can you remind us the requirement around data residency and KMS?
[02:49] Sanjay: customers in EU need residency at rest; we need to ensure KMS integration — BrightLoop uses Hashicorp Vault for keys and we'd like Redwood to support HSM-backed keys if possible for the private deployment.
[02:59] Mina: we have both KMS integrations and an HSM option for private deployments, but for hosted we can support customer-managed keys via our KMS bridge. I'll attach the security doc. Jordan: link?
[03:10] Jordan: yeah I'll send https://redwood.ai/docs/security/pilot-kms-hsm and the SOC2 summary.
[03:16] Leah: great. also on auditing, are you keeping per-token traces or just sampling? we need full audit trails for a week for compliance.
[03:24] Mina: we can capture full request/response logs but mask PII; by default we sample, but for pilots we can enable full retention for a bounded period. note this increases storage/ingest cost.
[03:36] Sanjay: acceptable if bounded to the pilot.
[03:38] Mina: noted.
[03:40] Jordan: can we talk about the two failure modes you saw? Mina listed serialization failure and KV cache misses. Mina, walk us through the timeline.
[03:48] Mina: sure. first failure: structured output serialization — happens when streaming + function-calling intersects with network jitter — results in truncated JSON and app retry. mitigation: 1) use SDK structured-output helper that does schema validation and reassembly; 2) on retry, fall back to a smaller text-only model to avoid function-call contract assumptions. second: KV cache miss storm — a burst of unique prefixes caused a rapid growth in KV writes and evictions, resulting in increased token generation as the model couldn't leverage cached prefixes. mitigation: set an eviction policy that favors recent convo state and enable local per-process prefix prefetching; also consider dedicated capacity for peak windows.
[04:33] Leah: can you explain the smaller-model fallback? is that like switching to an instruct-tiny model?
[04:38] Mina: exactly, switch to a cheaper variant for degraded conditions — for example, fallback from rdx-large-1 to rdx-medium-1 which is compatible for non-critical steps. the SDK supports policy-based routing: e.g., if p95 > 1.2s or error rate > 3%, route to fallback model.
[04:55] Marco: any impact on semantics when downgrading? product care about hallucinations.
[05:00] Mina: yes semantics can shift, so we recommend only using fallbacks for non-decision logic or for short recovery prompts. also use a checksum/validation step for any critical structured output.
[05:10] Jordan: coming back to telemetry — Mina you had a comparison table vs the BrightLoop in-app metrics?
[05:15] Mina: yes. we saw correlation on median but delta at p95. app-side saw retries and gRPC connection resets that redwood's runtime didn't mark as retries because they were client level. adding client-side trace correlation IDs will help us line up traces — we recommend stitch_id in headers.
[05:36] Leah: we'll pull those headers into our logs, good call.
[05:39] Sanjay: what about cost – we saw a higher than expected per-session cost because each short chat session opens a new conversation context. thoughts?
[05:48] Mina: two options: 1) reuse session context for quick follow ups to amortize the KV cache, or 2) use an explicit truncation policy so you don't keep long irrelevant history. both are implementable via the SDK; the runbook has config examples.
[06:02] Jordan: can we go over the telemetry artifacts you'll need from us to run the 24h stress?
[06:07] Mina: yes — at minimum: request id, stitch_id/correlation id, client-side latency, server-side latency, model variant, token counts, error codes, and the raw chunk trace for any truncated function calls. a zipped sample of 100 failure cases is very helpful.
[06:22] Leah: we can produce that. we'll anonymize PHI.
[06:25] Marco: timeline question — if the 24h run looks good, how quickly can we move to a small dedicated pool for pre-prod?
[06:31] Jordan: depends on sizing, but typically 2-3 weeks after we finalize peak RPS and footprint. Mina can lead a sizing session that uses the telemetry.
[06:39] Mina: yes I can run the sizing template and share the recommended GPU counts and burst config.
[06:44] Sanjay: ping on security review — we have a compliance committee next week. can we have an on-call SE to join for questions?
[06:51] Jordan: Mina can join the security review, and we'll send the KMS/HSM doc and SOC2 summary.
[06:57] Mina: also quick note on private deployment: if you want HSM-backed keys and network isolation, that path will require a bit longer lead time and an infra checklist — I'll attach it.
[07:07] Speaker 2: (laugh) we called it 'private cluster' last time and someone thought we meant on-prem bare metal.
[07:12] Marco: okay great to be explicit.
[07:14] Jordan: final QA — Marco any product concerns on function-calling semantics?
[07:18] Marco: only that we need deterministic mapping from model function name to our internal tool hooks. Mina's normalization suggestion should solve it. also a request: include a sample webhooks consumer for retry handling.
[07:29] Mina: we'll add that in the SDK examples.
[07:32] Jordan: quick recap — action items and owners, Jordan will share runbook and security links by Monday, Mina will draft fallback policy and batching config, Leah will run 24h stability and share traces, then we regroup after results. any other items?
[07:47] Sanjay: nope, looks good.
[07:49] Leah: thanks everyone.
[07:51] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up in slack and add the sizing session to the calendar for week of Oct 11.

References shared during call: https://redwood.ai/docs/integration/streaming-examples, https://redwood.ai/docs/security/pilot-kms-hsm, link to pilot benchmark sheet (internal) - "Pilot_Bench_2026_Q4.xlsx"

End of transcript.
